classification.classification_note: The witnessed failure is a 1-byte read past an undersized heap-allocated dummy luma row.

bug_description.original: The vulnerability occurs because jpeg_write_raw_data() expects the input size to be aligned to the MCU, but when image dimensions are not aligned, improper allocation of padded boundary rows happens. This misallocation affects the handling of boundary rows that require padding.
bug_description.normalized: The exact 9-byte witness `ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 ff` is tail-consumed by `FuzzedDataProvider` so that `muxSwitch == 0`, `width == 46` after even truncation, and `height == 262` after even truncation. Because those parses exhaust the witness, the later P010 stride booleans fall back false and the fuzzer stores `p010Img.luma_stride == 0` as the no-explicit-stride sentinel. API 0 `JpegR::encodeJPEGR` copies that struct, normalizes the sentinel, and tone-maps the HDR image into a temporary YUV420 buffer with `luma_stride = ALIGNM(width, 16) = 48`, so `JpegEncoderHelper::compressYuv` computes `need_padding == false`. Despite that aligned real-row stride, `compressYuv` allocates its fallback boundary row `empty` with only `cinfo->image_width` bytes, i.e. 46 bytes, instead of the aligned 48-byte width required by libjpeg's raw-data path. On the final iMCU row, missing bottom luma rows are replaced with `empty.get()` and passed directly to `jpeg_write_raw_data`. libjpeg's `forward_DCT` walks the row in 8-sample blocks, and the last block on a 46-pixel row starts at column 40; `convsamp` then performs eight fixed reads from offsets 40..47 and touches byte 46 one past the 46-byte allocation. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting heap-buffer-overflow in `convsamp`. The fix moves `aligned_width` earlier and sizes the `empty` allocation and zero-fill to that aligned width.

format.name: raw fuzzer blob for ultrahdr_enc_fuzzer
format.contract: The staged witness is exactly the 9-byte sequence `ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 ff`. Under `FuzzedDataProvider`'s tail-consuming semantics, the last byte `0xff` makes `muxSwitch == 0`; the next two remaining bytes `0x20 0x20` produce raw width 47, which line 120 truncates to `width == 46`; the final remaining leading byte `0xff` produces raw height 263, which line 123 truncates to `height == 262`. No bytes remain for the later bool/stride reads, so `ConsumeBool()` falls back to false, `p010Img.luma_stride` is stored as 0, and later `ConsumeIntegralInRange()` calls fall back to their minimum/default values. This GT is grounded only for that exact 9-byte witness and those decoded field values.

source.description: First project parse step that turns the attacker-controlled 9-byte blob into vulnerable-path control state. The tail byte `0xff` is consumed here and yields `muxSwitch == 0`, selecting the API-0 `JpegR::encodeJPEGR` path that reaches `JpegEncoderHelper::compressYuv`.
source.value_from: `poc` is the exact 9-byte blob `ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 ff`. `FuzzedDataProvider::ConsumeIntegralInRange()` consumes from the end of the remaining input, so the final byte `0xff` is read here and `0xff % 5 == 0` produces `muxSwitch == 0`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The fallback boundary-row buffer is allocated at `image_width` bytes instead of the aligned MCU width. For the witness this produces a 46-byte row even though the raw-data path later needs 48 bytes. The fix changes this allocation and the following zero-fill to `aligned_width`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. `convsamp` unconditionally reads eight samples from the selected row. On the witness's final dummy luma row with `start_col == 40`, that fixed 8-byte read touches offset 46 one byte past the 46-byte `empty` allocation.

tainted_value_origin.description: Concrete tainted size origin for the witness. With remaining bytes `20 20`, `FuzzedDataProvider` yields raw width 47 and the even-width normalization truncates it to `width == 46`, which later sizes the undersized `empty` allocation and determines the out-of-bounds read boundary.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: After the source step consumes the trailing selector byte, the next two remaining bytes are `0x20 0x20`, and `ConsumeIntegralInRange(8, 8192)` maps them to raw width 47 before line 120 truncates to even width 46.

parser_admitted.description: The staged 9-byte witness enters the project parser here: `FuzzedDataProvider` begins tail-consuming it into the API selector and then the width/height fields that drive the crashing encode path.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzzer helper tail-consumes the 9-byte witness into `muxSwitch == 0`, `width == 46`, and `height == 262`; with no bytes left for the later stride booleans, it writes those values into `p010Img` and stores the default `luma_stride == 0` sentinel before taking API 0.

API 0 copies `p010Img`, normalizes the zero luma-stride sentinel, builds a temporary YUV420 image with `luma_stride = ALIGNM(46, 16) = 48`, and passes the resulting width, height, and strides through `compressImage` into `setJpegCompressStruct` and `compressYuv`.

Inside `compressYuv`, the encoder allocates a 46-byte dummy boundary row, computes `aligned_width == 48` and `need_padding == false`, substitutes that dummy row for the missing bottom luma rows, and passes the raw planes directly to `jpeg_write_raw_data`.

libjpeg walks the final dummy luma row in 8-sample DCT blocks; the last block starts at column 40, and `convsamp`'s fixed 8-byte read crosses the 46-byte allocation boundary and triggers the ASan heap-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.code: UltraHdrEncFuzzer(const uint8_t* data, size_t size) : mFdp(data, size){};
fine_trace.note: The raw 9-byte witness is materialized as `FuzzedDataProvider` state. Subsequent `ConsumeIntegralInRange()` and `ConsumeBool()` calls in `process()` all derive their values from this same tail-consuming input cursor.
The last byte `0xff` is consumed from the witness tail, and `0xff % 5 == 0` produces `muxSwitch == 0`. That is the control value that later takes the API-0 `encodeJPEGR` arm seen in the crash stack.

The next two remaining bytes are `0x20 0x20`. `ConsumeIntegralInRange(8, 8192)` maps `0x2020` to raw width 47, then line 120 truncates it to the even witness width `46` that later sizes the dummy row and sets the final block boundary.

Only the leading byte `0xff` remains for the height read, so `ConsumeIntegralInRange(8, 8192)` produces raw height 263 and line 123 truncates it to the even witness height `262`. Because 262 is not a multiple of 16, the final iMCU row will need bottom boundary rows.

After the height read no bytes remain in the witness. The later bool reads therefore fall back false, so `hasYStride == false`, the ternary reuses `width`, and these assignments store the concrete carrier fields `p010Img.width == 46`, `p010Img.height == 262`, and `p010Img.luma_stride == 0` that API 0 later consumes.

The `muxSwitch == 0` arm is taken, and `encodeJPEGR()` receives the populated `p010Img` struct from step 5. The crash stack's `JpegR::encodeJPEGR(jpegr_uncompressed_struct*, ultrahdr_transfer_function, jpegr_compressed_struct*, int, jpegr_exif_struct*)` frame matches this exact call site.

fine_trace.var: p010_image.luma_stride, yu420_luma_stride, yuv420_image.width, yuv420_image.height, yuv420_image.luma_stride, yuv420_image.chroma_stride
fine_trace.note: API 0 copies the caller struct, normalizes the zero sentinel to `p010_image.luma_stride = p010_image.width = 46`, and creates the temporary YUV420 carrier with `width == 46`, `height == 262`, `luma_stride == ALIGNM(46, 16) == 48`, and `chroma_stride == 24`.
Those concrete temporary-image fields are passed into `JpegEncoderHelper::compressImage()`: width 46, height 262, `lumaStride == 48`, and `chromaStride == 24`.

Inside `encode()`, `setJpegCompressStruct(width, height, quality, &cinfo, uvBuffer == nullptr)` writes the forwarded dimensions into `cinfo`. Because step 8 passed a non-null `uvBuffer`, this is the raw YCbCr path with `cinfo->image_width == 46` and `cinfo->image_height == 262`.

`cinfo.num_components != 1` selects `compressYuv(&cinfo, yBuffer, uvBuffer, lumaStride, chromaStride)`, so `compressYuv` receives `cinfo->image_width == 46`, `cinfo->image_height == 262`, `lumaStride == 48`, and `chromaStride == 24`.

Root cause. `compressYuv` allocates the fallback boundary row at the unaligned visible width, so this witness gets only a 46-byte zero row. The patch changes this to `aligned_width`, which would be 48 for the same input.

fine_trace.code:
const int aligned_width = ALIGNM(cinfo->image_width, kCompressBatchSize);
const bool need_padding = (lumaStride < aligned_width);
fine_trace.note: With `cinfo->image_width == 46`, `aligned_width` becomes 48. Because `lumaStride == 48`, the predicate is false and the helper disables the `planes_intrm` padding path, so later fallback rows will be passed directly instead of being copied into an aligned intermediate buffer.

On the final loop iteration `cinfo->next_scanline` has reached 256 after prior 16-line batches. For `i >= 6`, `scanline >= 262`, so the missing bottom luma rows are replaced with `empty.get()`. Because `need_padding` is false, those row pointers are not widened through `y_intrm` and remain direct 46-byte dummy rows.

fine_trace.code:
int processed = jpeg_write_raw_data(cinfo, need_padding ? planes_intrm : planes,
                                    kCompressBatchSize);
fine_trace.note: The final iMCU row is submitted with `planes`, not `planes_intrm`, so libjpeg receives the raw luma row pointers from step 13, including the undersized `empty` rows for the bottom padding lines.

libjpeg processes the Y component in 8-sample DCT blocks. For `cinfo->image_width == 46`, that yields six horizontal luma blocks, so the last block reaches `start_col == 40` after the sequence 0, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40. `convsamp` is therefore invoked on the dummy row from step 13 with `start_col == 40`.

Sink. `convsamp` unconditionally performs eight reads from `sample_data[elemr] + start_col`. On the witness's dummy row with `start_col == 40`, those reads touch offsets 40..47; offset 46 is the first byte past the 46-byte `empty` allocation, matching ASan's reported 1-byte read immediately beyond `[0x...590, 0x...5be)`.
